title: Detailed protocol for germ-free Drosophila melanogaster colonization with Propionibacterium spp. biofilms
protocol: Heat and homogenize fly food ingredients in tap water, one at a time.
Stir the mixture until it boils and turn off the heat source.
Let the mixture cool down to 60°C.
Add 6 ml of p-Hydroxy-benzoic acid methyl ester diluted in 95% ethanol for each liter of media.
Add 10 mL of propionic acid to the media (for 1 L of media) and stir thoroughly.
Distribute 8 mL of media per vial manually and let cool down.
Cover vials with plastic wrap and store at 4°C until next step.
Work under sterile conditions from this point onwards.
Mix well by vortexing thoroughly.
Supplement the 8 mL of food with 1 mL of sterile sucrose.
Pipette the entire mixture to a new sterile vial.
Transfer Drosophila melanogaster in a starving vial and incubate for 6 hours at 25°C and 60% humidity.
Spray all materials with 70% ethanol before starting.
Perform all fruit flies’ manipulations in a BSC using sterile media.
Start the experiment with young fruit flies (<3 days old).
Place the vial on ice to anesthetize fruit flies.
Wash fruit flies with a sterile washing kit.
Add 2 mL of 70% ethanol to the vial and quickly filter fruit flies through a cell strainer.
Immerse the cell strainer for 2 min in a Petri dish containing 2.7% sodium hypochlorite.
Flush with 70% ethanol.
Immerse the cell strainer with the fruit flies for 10 min in autoclaved milli-Q water.
Place the cell strainer on blotting paper to absorb excess water.
Let the fruit flies air dry in the BSC by covering the cell strainer with an empty vial until they no longer stick together or to surfaces (approximately 10 min).
Transfer fruit flies into an empty sterile vial to recover for between 15–30 minutes.
Transfer fruit flies into a vial containing 2 mL BHIAgsy supplemented with antibiotics.
Transfer fruit flies when they are fully conscious and mobile.
Place vials sideways to let the fruit flies recover.
Incubate for 18–24 h at 25°C and 60% humidity.
Collect and dechorionated fruit flies’ eggs with a new washing kit.
Remove fruit flies from the vial.
Add 2 ml of sterile water.
Gently brush the surface of the media to collect eggs.
Transfer the mixture (water and eggs) into a cell strainer.
Wash eggs in the cell strainer.
Immerse the cell strainer in a Petri dish containing 2,7% sodium hypochlorite for 2 min.
Wash with 70% ethanol.
Immerse the cell strainer into a Petri dish with water for 10 min.
Take out the cell strainer from the water.
Transfer washed eggs with a plastic transfer pipette to fresh autoclaved modified Bloomington food supplemented with antibiotics.
Incubate the vial at 25°C and 60% humidity until new fruit flies hatch.
Repeat two more-time steps 15–25 starting with the newly hatched fruit flies from step 25.
Collect young fruit flies each day into a BHIAgsy vial supplemented with antibiotics when pupa start to hatch.
Continue collecting fruit flies for three days before repeating step 15.
After three generations (G1, G2, G3), consider the fruit flies sterile and ready as an in vivo model.
Maintain and cross GF fruit flies on sterile food with antibiotics until the desired number of young GF fruit flies is reached.
Slightly scratch the surface of frozen Propionibacterium spp. glycerol stock with a sterile inoculating loop.
Streak the loop across a blood agar plate.
Invert and incubate the plates at 37°C for 72 hours anaerobically.
Pick-up one colony from the plate with a sterile inoculating loop.
Inoculate 10 mL of BHIg with the picked colony.
Incubate the BHIg at 37°C with 250 rpm agitation for 48 hours anaerobically.
Inoculated 9.5 mL of BHIg in a T-25 cell culture flask with 500 μL of the preculture.
Incubate the flask horizontally at 37°C for 6 days anaerobically.
Change the medium every 48 hours during incubation.
Tilt the flask for about 10 minutes between 18°C and 25°C to let the biofilm pelleted at the corner of the flask by gravity.
Carefully pipette the supernatant (about 8 ml) without disturbing the pellet.
Discard the removed supernatant.
Add slowly 10 ml of BHIg.
Transfer fruit flies two times for 24 hours on BHIAgsy supplemented with antibiotics.
Incubate at 25°C and 60% humidity.
Transfer fruit flies onto BHIAgsy without antibiotics and incubate for 24 hours.
Recover 6-day-old biofilm of Propionibacterium spp. formed at the bottom of the T-25 culture flask.
Tilt the flask by ± 45° angle for about 10 minutes to let the biofilm pelleted by gravity.
Pipette slowly 1 mL of the biofilm from the corner of the flask and transfer it to a sterile 1.5 mL micro-tube.
Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 1,150 g between 18°C and 25°C.
Discard the supernatant by pipetting.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of BHIs by pipetting up and down.
Pipette 100 μL of the concentrated biofilm suspension onto the filter of an infection vial.
Let the filter dry/absorb for 30 minutes.
Transfer fruit flies from step 31.c and incubate for 24 hours.
Repeat the infection procedure using the fruit flies from step 33 every 24 hours for 6 days.
After 6 days of infection, transfer the fruit flies onto BHIAgsy without antibiotics and incubate for 24 hours.
Anesthetize fruit flies on ice.
Place them into a fine pore tissue cassette using forceps.
Place the small cassette in a larger tissue embedding cassette.
Immerse the fruit flies in buffered formalin or fixative alternative for at least 12 hours.
Rinse the fruit flies two times for 10 minutes each with PBS 1X.
Transfer the tissue embedding cassettes through serial baths of ethanol: Two baths of 70% ethanol, one bath of 80% ethanol, and one bath of 90% ethanol, each lasting one hour.
Dilute absolute ethanol in sterile milli-Q water to freshly prepare 70%, 80%, and 90% ethanol solutions.
Perform tissue dehydration by immersing the samples in three baths of each ethanol concentration for 1.5 hours.
Clear tissues with three baths of Xylene for 1.5 hours each.
Infiltrate the tissue with paraffin by immersing the sample two times for 2 hours in paraffin wax at 58°C–60°C.
Embed the sample in a paraffin block using stainless steel embedding molds.
Trim excess paraffin from around fruit flies to optimize section placement on slides.
Place sections correctly within circles drawn after deparaffinization for immunofluorescence staining.
Place fruit flies on the slide for visualization without processing.
Cut FFPE blocks at 4 μm using a microtome.
Transfer each section to a 45°C water bath using fine forceps.
Pick up floating sections with highly adhesive slides for immunofluorescence or regular slides if unprocessed visualization is planned.
Place the slides from step 45 on a slide staining rack.
Melt the paraffin by incubating the slides at 60°C for 1 h.
Immerse the slides two times for 10 min in xylene to deparaffinize.
Rehydrate by immersing the slides in 100% ethanol for 2 min.
Immerse slides in 70% ethanol for 2 minutes.
Immerse slides in 30% ethanol for 2 minutes.
Wash the slides by immersing the rack two times for 5 minutes each in PBS 1X.
Draw a circle with a hydrophobic barrier pen around slide-mounted tissue to create a water-repellent barrier.
Incubate hydrated tissue sections with proteinase K (25 μg/mL) at 37°C for 15 minutes.
Add normal horse serum blocking solution and incubate between 18°C and 25°C for 20 minutes.
Apply the primary antibody on the fruit flies’ tissues and incubate for 1 hour between 18°C and 25°C.
Wash the slides by immersing the rack two times for 5 min in PBS 1X.
Apply the secondary antibody and incubate for 1 h between 18°C and 25°C in a moist chamber, protected from light.
Wash the slides by immersing the rack two times for 5 min in PBS 1X.
Add a drop of DAPI (4 μg/mL) on fruit flies’ tissues and incubate for 2 min.
Add a drop of glycerol/PBS antifade solution.
Cover the sample with a coverslip starting from one side and quickly applying it to avoid air bubbles.
Seal the edges with a coverslip sealant.
Store the slides in darkness at 4°C.
Take an image of the slides as soon as possible.
Capture images using an epifluorescence or confocal microscope using appropriate wavelength.
Use DAPI and secondary antibodies with Alexa Fluor 488, 555, 647 to label the samples.
Analyze immunostained sections on a Zeiss Axio Imager M2 microscope using 10×/0.3, 20×/0.8 and 63×/1.4 oil objectives.
Capture images with a Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash 4.0 LT digital CMOS camera.

Visualize DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, 555, and 647 simultaneously in each slide using Zeiss Filter Set 01 (ex: BP 365/12, em: LP39738), HE (Ex: 470/40, Em: 525/50), 43 (Ex: 545/25, Em: 605/70) and 50 (Ex: 640/30, Em: 690/50).
Process images using the ZEN software.
Observe unprocessed slides with a light microscope when procedure has been validated with immunofluorescence.
